overview: Case-control study nested in adults treated for hip fracture on the trauma unit from January 2022 to December 2024.
population: Eligible: adults aged 60 and over with surgery for hip fracture who survived to discharge. Cases: 80 patients sampled at random from those with a stay longer than 28 days. Controls: 160 patients with a stay of 28 days or less, frequency matched by year and operation type.
exposure: First mobilisation within 24 hours of the end of surgery, defined as standing or walking with a physiotherapist, read from the physiotherapy entry with the nursing entry as a check; reason for delay recorded.
procedures: The clerical team pulls the paper notes; two readers (a senior physiotherapist and a trained clerical officer) use a written form; stay length is hidden on the reading sheet; 10 percent of notes are read twice.

outcomes.name: Stay longer than 28 days
outcomes.measure: Discharge more than 28 days after admission, from the unit's hip fracture list; defines case status
outcomes.why: Long stays are what patients, families and planners feel.

outcomes.name: Discharge destination
outcomes.measure: Return to the pre-fracture residence against a new care placement
outcomes.why: Matters to patients as much as stay length.

outcomes.name: Exposure readable
outcomes.measure: Proportion of sampled notes with a documented time of first mobilisation
outcomes.why: Unreadable notes would bias the exposure.

feasibility: 240 notes at about 25 minutes each use the 100 approved hours.
biasMitigation: Adjustment set limited to pre-surgical characteristics, fixed before reading
Postoperative hypotension and delirium in a sensitivity analysis only
Weekend-delay subgroup as a check on confounding

biasFlags.label: Confounding by indication
biasFlags.note: Sicker patients are mobilised later and stay longer.

biasFlags.label: Over-adjustment
biasFlags.note: Postoperative conditions may lie on the causal path.

flags: Five pre-surgical covariates plus two matching factors
parsimony.simplestPath: One exposure, one outcome, one adjusted logistic model.

theoreticalFramework: A directed acyclic graph drawn before reading to separate pre-surgical confounders from postoperative conditions on the causal path.
summary: Case-control study of 80 cases and 160 controls with pre-surgical adjustment and a confounding check.
